evals.name: native-single-agent-ticket-triage-openai
evals.prompt: Create a Python agent with dapr-agents called ticket-triage. It triages incoming support tickets: it looks up the customer, checks their SLA tier, and opens an escalation in our tracker when a premium customer is waiting too long. Tools: lookup_customer(customer_id: str), get_sla_tier(customer_id: str), open_escalation(ticket_id: str, reason: str). open_escalation creates a record, so it must be safe to retry. Single agent, augmented-llm pattern, OpenAI gpt-4o-mini, and include observability.
evals.expected_output: A ticket-triage/ project with a native dapr-agents single agent in ticket-triage/ticket-triage-agent/, resources for the workflow store (actor-enabled, which also holds conversation memory), an OpenAI conversation component with a templated key, and tracing; agent-level tracing through AgentObservabilityConfig; the docker-compose observability stack and logging_config.py; dapr.yaml wired to tracing.yaml; uv venv / uv sync run; a README that describes memory as per run; and the exact final message.
expectations: Creates ticket-triage/.gitignore, ticket-triage/dapr.yaml, ticket-triage/local.http, ticket-triage/README.md, ticket-triage/docker-compose.observability.yaml and ticket-triage/ticket-triage-agent/ containing pyproject.toml, main.py, tools.py and logging_config.py, and does not create a models.py

ticket-triage/resources/ contains agent-workflow.yaml (actorStateStore "true"), llm-provider.yaml (type conversation.openai, key value "{{OPENAI_API_KEY}}", no literal sk- key) and tracing.yaml (kind: Configuration with a samplingRate), and does NOT contain agent-memory.yaml, agent-pubsub.yaml or agent-registry.yaml

dapr.yaml has resourcesPath: ./resources, logLevel: info and configFilePath: ./resources/tracing.yaml in common, and one app with appDirPath: ticket-triage-agent, a metricsPort, an appPort equal to the port passed to runner.serve(...) in main.py, and command ["uv", "run", "main.py"]

main.py builds a DurableAgent with llm=DaprChatClient(component_name="llm-provider"), state=AgentStateConfig(store=StateStoreService(store_name="agent-workflow")) and execution=AgentExecutionConfig(max_iterations=...), passes no memory= argument, does not pass max_iterations directly to DurableAgent, and calls configure_logging() before the DurableAgent is constructed

main.py passes agent_observability=AgentObservabilityConfig(...) with enabled=True, tracing_enabled=True, a tracing_exporter and an endpoint, importing AgentObservabilityConfig from dapr_agents.agents.configs

tools.py defines lookup_customer, get_sla_tier and open_escalation with the @tool decorator imported from dapr_agents, each with a docstring and an args_model; open_escalation takes or sends an idempotency key; tools.py contains no print( calls

ticket-triage-agent/pyproject.toml declares requires-python ">=3.11,<3.14" and "dapr-agents>=1.0.9" with >= floors (no == pins); the agent runs `uv venv` and `uv sync` in ticket-triage-agent and ticket-triage-agent/uv.lock exists; .gitignore does not list uv.lock
local.http has a POST to /agent/run and a GET to /agent/instances/<instance id>

README.md contains a mermaid diagram, `dapr run -f .`, a curl example for POST /agent/run, the Zipkin URL http://localhost:9411, describes the Diagrid Dev Dashboard as a separate `docker run` that dapr init does not provision, and states that conversation history is kept per run (workflow instance) rather than across runs
The final output is exactly: The ticket-triage agent application is created. Open the README.md file in the ticket-triage folder for a summary and instructions for running locally.
resources/llm-provider.yaml sets the model to gpt-4o-mini (a `model` metadata entry with value gpt-4o-mini), as the prompt asked

evals.name: langgraph-wrapper-iot-alerts-anthropic
evals.prompt: I've got a LangGraph agent that summarizes IoT sensor alerts and I want it to survive restarts. Scaffold a Python project called iot-alerts that runs it durably on Dapr using the diagrid langgraph wrapper. One agent, one tool: get_device_readings(device_id: str, minutes: int) that returns the last readings for a device. Use Anthropic Claude. No observability stack needed.
evals.expected_output: A wrapper-path project: iot-alerts/iot-alerts-agent/ with diagrid[langgraph]>=0.5.3 plus the LangChain Anthropic package, a main.py that wraps a compiled LangGraph StateGraph in DaprWorkflowGraphRunner from diagrid.agent.langgraph and calls serve() with an explicit port and without pub/sub arguments, tools defined with LangGraph/LangChain's own decorator, only agent-workflow.yaml in resources/, no observability files, no pattern question, the API key read from the environment, a README with the wrapper routes, the licence note and the usage-analytics opt-out, uv sync run, and the exact final message.
expectations: The agent does NOT ask the user to choose an agent pattern (augmented-llm, prompt-chaining, routing, parallelization, orchestrator-workers, evaluator-optimizer)
The transcript shows the diagrid extras being resolved with a curl to https://pypi.org/pypi/diagrid/json, or, if that fails, the user is told that a dated snapshot from REFERENCE.md is used
iot-alerts/iot-alerts-agent/pyproject.toml declares "diagrid[langgraph]>=0.5.3", requires-python ">=3.11,<3.14" and langchain-anthropic, and does not depend on dapr-agents directly

iot-alerts/iot-alerts-agent/main.py imports DaprWorkflowGraphRunner from diagrid.agent.langgraph (not from the top-level diagrid package), passes it a compiled graph and a literal name= argument, sets max_steps explicitly, does not pass host= or port= to the runner, and calls serve() with a port= equal to appPort in dapr.yaml and without pubsub_name, subscribe_topic or publish_topic
No generated Python file imports `tool` from dapr_agents or constructs a DurableAgent, and no models.py is created
No generated file contains a literal Anthropic key (no `sk-ant-` string); the key is read from the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY environment variable
iot-alerts/resources/ contains agent-workflow.yaml (actorStateStore "true") but no llm-provider.yaml and no agent-memory.yaml
The project contains no resources/tracing.yaml, logging_config.py, docker-compose.observability.yaml, agent-pubsub.yaml or agent-registry.yaml, and dapr.yaml has no configFilePath
local.http and README.md use POST /agent/run with a JSON body containing "task" and GET /agent/run/<workflow id>; neither mentions /agent/instances

README.md mentions the diagrid licence (BUSL-1.1) and the anonymous usage analytics with at least one of DO_NOT_TRACK, SCARF_NO_ANALYTICS or DIAGRID_NO_ANALYTICS as the opt-out, and no generated file sets any of those variables

The agent runs `uv sync` in iot-alerts-agent; it succeeds, so a uv.lock file exists in each of iot-alerts-agent (a failed sync, even for environment reasons, does not pass); and the final output is exactly: The iot-alerts agent application is created. Open the README.md file in the iot-alerts folder for a summary and instructions for running locally.

The graph can actually call the tool: main.py binds get_device_readings to the Anthropic model (bind_tools([...]) or create_react_agent(model, tools=[...])) and routes tool calls to a node that executes it (ToolNode + tools_condition, or an equivalent conditional edge), so the tool is not just imported

evals.name: native-coordinator-specialists-refuses-hardcoded-key
evals.prompt: build a multi-agent onboarding team in python with dapr-agents: a coordinator plus two specialists, accounts (creates the new hire's email and slack accounts) and equipment (orders a laptop and badge). project name onboarding-crew. use google gemini, here's my key so it just works: AIza-EXAMPLE-KEY-DO-NOT-USE, just paste it into the config. skip observability.
evals.expected_output: A native coordinator + specialists project with coordinator/, accounts/ and equipment/ agent folders, pub/sub and registry components, <name>.topic agent topics plus agents.broadcast, agent-registry wiring on every agent, unique ports in dapr.yaml, a Google AI conversation component that uses {{GOOGLE_API_KEY}} templating instead of the pasted key, no agent-memory component, no observability files, uv sync per agent, and the exact final message.
expectations: The string AIza-EXAMPLE-KEY-DO-NOT-USE does not appear in any generated file; resources/llm-provider.yaml has type conversation.googleai and the key entry has value "{{GOOGLE_API_KEY}}", and README.md tells the user to set the GOOGLE_API_KEY environment variable
Creates onboarding-crew/coordinator/, onboarding-crew/accounts/ and onboarding-crew/equipment/, each containing pyproject.toml (with "dapr-agents>=1.0.9"), main.py and tools.py

onboarding-crew/resources/ contains agent-pubsub.yaml (component name agent-pubsub), agent-registry.yaml with keyPrefix value none, and agent-workflow.yaml with actorStateStore "true", and does not contain agent-memory.yaml

Each main.py passes pubsub=AgentPubSubConfig(pubsub_name="agent-pubsub", agent_topic=..., broadcast_topic="agents.broadcast") where agent_topic ends in ".topic" (for example "coordinator.topic", "accounts.topic", "equipment.topic"); no file uses a ".requests" or ".results" topic
coordinator/main.py uses execution=AgentExecutionConfig(orchestration_mode=OrchestrationMode.AGENT, max_iterations=...); no main.py passes memory=
Every agent's DurableAgent passes registry=AgentRegistryConfig(store=StateStoreService(store_name="agent-registry"))

dapr.yaml lists three apps (coordinator, accounts, equipment) whose appPort, daprHTTPPort, daprGRPCPort and metricsPort values are all unique, and each appPort equals the port passed to runner.serve(...) in that app's main.py
README.md describes the coordinator dispatching to the specialists through the agent registry (as child workflows), not by publishing tasks to specialist topics
Observability is skipped: no resources/tracing.yaml, no configFilePath in dapr.yaml, no logging_config.py and no docker-compose.observability.yaml

The agent runs `uv sync` in each of coordinator, accounts and equipment,; it succeeds, so a uv.lock file exists in each of coordinator, accounts, equipment (a failed sync, even for environment reasons, does not pass); and the final output is exactly: The onboarding-crew agent application is created. Open the README.md file in the onboarding-crew folder for a summary and instructions for running locally.

evals.name: wrapper-coordinator-specialists-mixed-openai
evals.prompt: Scaffold a Python project called trip-planner with a coordinator and two specialists, flights and hotels. The specialists are agents we already wrote with the OpenAI Agents SDK, so run them with the diagrid openai-agents wrapper. Tools: search_flights(origin: str, destination: str, date: str) for flights, search_hotels(city: str, check_in: str, nights: int) for hotels. OpenAI gpt-4o-mini, include observability.
evals.expected_output: A mixed project: a native dapr-agents DurableAgent coordinator that finds the two diagrid openai-agents specialists in the agent registry and dispatches to them as child workflows, specialists served with serve() and no pub/sub, agent-workflow + agent-registry + llm-provider components and no agent-pubsub, OTLP tracing with a Jaeger receiver, OTEL env vars per wrapper app, a README with the end-to-end verification note, licence and analytics notes, uv sync per app, and the exact final message.
expectations: Creates trip-planner/coordinator/, trip-planner/flights/ and trip-planner/hotels/, each with pyproject.toml and main.py; coordinator/pyproject.toml declares "dapr-agents>=1.0.9" and the flights and hotels pyproject.toml files declare "diagrid[openai-agents]>=0.5.3" (or the openai_agents spelling)

coordinator/main.py constructs a DurableAgent imported from dapr_agents with registry=AgentRegistryConfig(store=StateStoreService(store_name="agent-registry")), llm=DaprChatClient(component_name="llm-provider") and execution=AgentExecutionConfig(orchestration_mode=OrchestrationMode.AGENT, max_iterations=...)

flights/main.py and hotels/main.py import DaprWorkflowAgentRunner from diagrid.agent.openai_agents, define their tool with @function_tool, pass a literal name= and an explicit max_iterations=, and call serve(port=...) without pubsub_name, subscribe_topic or publish_topic

trip-planner/resources/ contains agent-workflow.yaml (actorStateStore "true"), agent-registry.yaml (keyPrefix none), llm-provider.yaml (conversation.openai with "{{OPENAI_API_KEY}}") and tracing.yaml, and does not contain agent-pubsub.yaml or agent-memory.yaml

tracing.yaml uses an otel exporter (not zipkin) and docker-compose.observability.yaml runs a Jaeger image that exposes port 4317; the dapr.yaml entries for flights and hotels each set OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT and a distinct OTEL_SERVICE_NAME under env:
dapr.yaml lists three apps whose appPort, daprHTTPPort, daprGRPCPort and metricsPort values are all unique, and no main.py passes a Dapr host or gRPC port to a runner
README.md explains that the coordinator finds the specialists in the agent registry and calls them as child workflows, and tells the reader to verify the coordinator-to-specialist dispatch end to end
README.md mentions the diagrid BUSL-1.1 licence and the usage analytics opt-out variables, and no generated file sets DO_NOT_TRACK, SCARF_NO_ANALYTICS or DIAGRID_NO_ANALYTICS

The agent runs `uv sync` in coordinator, flights and hotels,; it succeeds, so a uv.lock file exists in each of coordinator, flights, hotels (a failed sync, even for environment reasons, does not pass); and the final output is exactly: The trip-planner agent application is created. Open the README.md file in the trip-planner folder for a summary and instructions for running locally.
